sumInsured: As per Policy Schedule (not provided in extract)

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: The Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year
great.explanation: Your base Sum Insured is automatically reinstated unlimited times within the same policy year after it is used up. This means you get continuous coverage without waiting for a new policy year.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness except for claim under Any one Illness condition.
great.explanation: The restored Sum Insured can be used for the same illness except under the 'Any One Illness' condition. This gives you more flexibility than restores limited only to unrelated illnesses.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: For any single Claim during a Policy Year, the maximum Claim amount payable shall be sum total of Sum Insured, Cumulative Bonus, Inflation Shield.
great.reference: Clause 3, General Conditions Applicable To All The Benefits, point 2(II)
great.explanation: Additional Sum Insured buffers like Cumulative Bonus and Inflation Shield increase your coverage beyond the base Sum Insured. This provides extra financial protection during claims.

great.name: No Claim Bonus
great.quote: enhance the Sum Insured by 50% flat, on a cumulative basis... provided that no Claim has been paid... or total claim amount payable does not exceed the 25% of the base Sum Insured
great.reference: Clause 3.1.11 Benefit : No Claim Bonus Protect
great.explanation: You get a 50% increase in your Sum Insured as a renewal bonus if no claims are paid or claims are below 25% of the base Sum Insured. This rewards claim-free years with significant coverage increases.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded for 36 months from your first policy start date. This is a reasonable waiting period common in the market.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Specified illnesses have a 24-month waiting period before coverage begins. This is standard practice for certain conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered during the first 30 days of the policy, except for accidents. This is a common initial waiting period.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Under Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 60 days immediately prior
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps cover diagnostic and treatment costs before admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Under Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 90 days immediately after
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 90 days after discharge are covered, providing good support for follow-up care.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: If the Policy Schedule states ‘up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day’ as eligible Room Rent, it means the maximum eligible Room Rent... is limited to 1% of the Sum Insured per day of Hospitalization.
bad.explanation: Room rent is capped at 1% of the Sum Insured per day, which can cause significant out-of-pocket costs if you choose a higher category room.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: The Policyholder/Insured Person shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses... in the proportion of the difference between the Room Rent actually incurred and the Room Rent specified in the Policy Schedule
bad.explanation: If you stay in a room above your eligibility, the insurer reduces payouts on related medical expenses proportionally, increasing your expenses.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – I to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.explanation: Common consumables like gloves and masks are excluded, meaning you may have to pay for these during hospitalization.

bad.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
bad.quote: Any Medical Expenses incurred for the treatment in relation to any of the following diseases shall not be payable under this Benefit : ... Diabetes Mellitus... Hypertension... Arthritis...
bad.explanation: Many common chronic diseases are excluded from domiciliary hospitalization benefits, limiting the usefulness of this coverage.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: For diseases or conditions or procedure that have a specified sub-limit then all related expenses shall be covered up to the sub-limit specified for that disease or condition or procedure.
bad.explanation: The policy applies sub-limits on certain diseases or procedures, which can reduce claim payouts significantly.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: The Co-payment proportion (if applicable)... The Policy Schedule will specify the Optional Benefits that are in force
bad.explanation: The base co-pay percentage is not clearly stated and may depend on optional covers or your Policy Schedule. Confirm your co-pay details in your policy documents.

unclear.name: Room Rent Eligibility
unclear.quote: The Policy Schedule will specify the eligibility of Room Rent or Room Category applicable
unclear.explanation: The exact room rent eligibility depends on your Policy Schedule. This affects your claim amount if you choose a higher room category.

unclear.name: NCB Reduction
unclear.quote: In the event of total claim amount payable exceeds 25% of the base Sum Insured during any Policy Year, the accrued Cumulative Bonus will be reduced at same rate at which it is accrued
unclear.explanation: The No Claim Bonus reduces proportionally if claims exceed 25% of the base Sum Insured, but the exact impact depends on your claim amounts and policy details.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
